focus: Remaining five Priority-1 Poaceae queue items: four training cards plus one Bothriochloa taxonomy resolution

taxonomy_resolution.resolution: Do not build as a separate Texas learner card pending source reconciliation.
rationale: POWO 2026 accepts Bothriochloa torreyana as native in Texas.
POWO treats Bothriochloa laguroides subsp. torreyana as a synonym of B. torreyana.
POWO's accepted B. laguroides sensu stricto is native from Mexico southward and not native to Texas.
Texas/older regional sources often use B. laguroides subsp. torreyana for silver bluestem.
taxonomy_resolution.canonical_action: Keep the Master Plant Pool source row on taxonomy hold until Hays/NPSOT source names are reconciled; use existing curated B. torreyana as the learner anchor.

cards.look_here_first: Find one mature floret and follow the single very long awn. It is one-awned, not three-awned.
confirm: Cool-season perennial bunchgrass with an open, wispy panicle.
One-flowered spikelets with glumes longer than the floret.
Lemma terminates in one very long awn, commonly twice-geniculate with a twisted basal column.
Nodes are commonly pubescent; sheaths can be conspicuously hairy.
Ligule is short and membranous; collars can have small tufts of hairs at the sides.
cards.tie_breaker: Aristida typically presents three awns from the lemma; Nassella leucotricha has one conspicuous long twisted/bent awn.
cards.local_relevance: UT Hays County flora directly documents Nassella leucotricha in northern Hays County.

cards.look_here_first: Before flowering, go straight to the collar: look for the paired pointed 'rabbit-ear' or 'gun-sight' auricles/horns.
confirm: Tall warm-season perennial from short scaly rhizomes.
Collar region has conspicuous pointed auricle-like horns flanking a membranous ligule.
Nodes are often hairy.
Panicle is golden/bronze and relatively contracted.
Fertile spikelets are one-flowered, hairy, and carry a twisted bent awn.
cards.tie_breaker: Indiangrass has the distinctive upright rabbit-ear/gun-sight structures at the collar; switchgrass instead has a dense white hairy ligule/collar zone.

cards.look_here_first: Look for the narrow, spike-like contracted panicle that is often partly hidden inside the upper leaf sheath.
confirm: Perennial tufted bunchgrass with stout erect culms.
Ligule is extremely short, essentially a ciliate line/fringe.
Panicle branches are appressed, making the inflorescence look spike-like; the base is commonly enclosed by the subtending sheath.
Spikelets are one-flowered, laterally compressed and awnless.
Glumes are unequal; lemma is smooth in typical S. compositus and the palea is about as long as the lemma.
cards.tie_breaker: Against S. clandestinus, use smooth vs hairy lemma/sheath characters plus panicle/spikelet dimensions; Central Texas material may require microscopic lemma characters or wet-pericarp testing.
cards.caution: The S. compositus complex is genuinely difficult in Texas. UT herbarium work documents disagreement even among expert determinations; do not force variety-level IDs from habit alone.

cards.look_here_first: Go straight to the thick corn-like flowering branch: hard bead-like female joints are below and dangling male spikelets/anthers are above.
confirm: Huge rhizomatous clump with very broad rough-edged leaves and a strong pale midrib.
Ligule is a short ciliate or ciliate-membranous structure; sheaths are open.
Plant is monoecious, with female and male spikelets separated along the same flowering branch.
Female spikelets are sunken into hard cylindrical/bony joints that break apart at maturity.
Male spikelets occur above, often in pairs, with conspicuous dangling anthers.
cards.tie_breaker: No other common local grass combines the huge broad-leaved clump with stacked hard female joints below and male spikelets above on the same thick branch.

key_new_comparisons: Aristida purpurea (3 awns) vs Nassella leucotricha (1 long twisted awn)
Panicum virgatum hairy white collar vs Sorghastrum nutans rabbit-ear/gun-sight collar horns
Sporobolus compositus vs S. clandestinus requires fine lemma/pericarp characters
